title: NIST AI 600-1: Generative AI Risk Profile — What UK Deployers Need to Know
hook: NIST released AI 600-1 in July 2024 as a dedicated risk management profile for generative AI. By September 2026, UK deployers mapping against DSIT's pro-innovation framework find 600-1 is the de facto reference for hallucination, data-poisoning, and content-authenticity risks.
answer_first: NIST AI 600-1 extends the AI RMF (AI 600-1) with generative-specific risks: confabulation/hallucination, training-data poisoning, sensitive data disclosure, and content authenticity gaps. UK organisations can use 600-1 as a voluntary supplement to the EU AI Act Article 9 risk-management obligations and the UK's sector-specific regulatory approach. Council's verified measurement credential maps directly onto 600-1's measurement controls.
council_position: Council of AI treats NIST AI 600-1 as a baseline risk taxonomy. Every Council measurement includes a hallucination-rate proxy, a data-provenance check, and a content-authenticity flag — all 600-1 aligned. Measured containment is the operational layer that turns 600-1's descriptive risks into auditable metrics.
